ORAL ORDER 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 20.3.2024 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (Aux.VI), Ahmedabad (R), Navrangpura in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.942 of 2017, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Rs.23,02,778/- with 9% p.a. interest to be paid to claimant/s, by holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.

2. The facts of the present appeal are as under :

The claimants filed the claim petition before the learned Tribunal stating that the Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Surajben Hathibhai Patel on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88442330/

sentences.text:
1 deceased was going on his motorcycle no.GJ-09-AM-7912 from Chiloda to Himmatnagar road, at about 8.30 p.m. in the evening, when the deceased was passing near Ambaji Mata temple situated at Giyod village on national highway no.8,
at that time, the opponent no.1 came over driving his vehicle tractor no.GJ-18D-6515 in full speed, rashly and negligently, violating the traffic rules, without giving any signal of horn and dashed it to the motorcycle of deceased, due to which the deceased fell down on the road and sustained serious injuries and fractures over the head and also sustained other fatal injuries over different body parts and succumbed on the spot because of the injuries sustained in the alleged vehicular accident.

The FIR was lodged at Chiloda police station, Dist.Gandhinagar against the driver of the tractor-opponent no.1.
2.2
The notices were served to the opponents.
The opponents filed the written statement before the learned Tribunal.
The issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led before the Tribunal.

After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2236/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined 2.3
Hence, the insurance company of the tractor involved in the accident has filed the present appeal before this Court.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant - Insurance Company has submitted that as there was head-on collision between the motorcycle and the tractors, the drivers of both the vehicles ought to have been held equally liable to the accident and the learned Tribunal has erred in holding the tractor negligent to the extent of 80%.
He also submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation and the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the multiplier of five only.
He also submitted that the rate of interest awarded at the 9% is also on the higher side and the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded 7.5%.
He submitted that on all these counts, this appeal is required to be allowed and the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified.
4. I have considered the submissions made by the the learned advocate for the appellant.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the pleadings of the parties before the Tribunal.

Considering the FIR, panchanama of scene of offence, PM report, inquest panchanama, wherein it is clear that there was head-on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2236/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined collision between the two vehicles, the driver of the tractor did not enter into the witness box to contradict the say of the complainant, the injuries were sustained by the deceased which led to death of the deceased and that though it is a case of contributory negligence, as the tractor was a heavy vehicle, the negligence was apportioned at 80% to the tractor and 20% to the motorcycle.

5. It is now well settled that multiplier is to be based on age of the deceased in view of the judgment in the case of Joginder Singh V/s ICICI Lombard reported in 2020(18)SCC 808, Rakesh Arora V/s Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Surajben Hathibhai Patel on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88442330/

sentences.text: 2 Bharti Axa General Ins.co.Ltd. Reported in 2023 ACJ 337 and Bheemasen Since Deceased Through His Lrs. V/s Aravind Bangar reported in 2024 ACJ 221 and therefore, the multiplier of 15 years awarded for age of 37 years of deceased is just and proper.

sentences.text: Further, considering the proof of income of the deceased produced on the record, his age, number of dependents, future prospects, law laid down with regard to the multiplier and conventional heads, the learned Tribunal has awarded the amount of compensation.

6. As regards the ground of rate of interest on the awarded amount, there are several instances where the learned Tribunal has awarded 9% interest and that there is no hard and fast rule to award the rate of interest.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2236/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined

Considering the year of accident and considering the nature of the work done by the deceased and his dependents and also considering the other surrounding circumstances, the Court may exercise discretion without assigning any further reasons.
Normally, the interest rate which is awarded by the Courts in the motor accident claim petitions in the last few years is between 6% to 9% p.a.
Therefore, it cannot be said that where the interest is already awarded at 9% should now be reduced in this appeal.
7. In view of above discussion and as the insurance company has failed to prove its case by leading cogent and convincing reasons, this appeal therefore deserves to be dismissed at admission stage.
8. In view of above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal and civil application are dismissed with no order as to costs.
8.2 The appellant is directed to deposit the entire awarded amount with costs and interest before the concerned Tribunal within four weeks from today.

After the amount is deposited, the learned Tribunal shall pass the order of disbursement as per the operative portion of the impugned judgment and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2236/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined award within a period of six weeks thereafter.
8.3 Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
